description: Original paper figures, displayed in full and available for larger viewing. WebP files are lossless, pixel-identical conversions of the sourced originals.

figures.alt: Original HyperAdaLoRA framework comparing LoRA, AdaLoRA, and hypernetwork-generated low-rank components.
figures.reason: The paper’s original three-panel framework comparison directly illustrates the proposed hypernetwork rank-adaptation method. Extracted complete figure from PDF page 2, preserving all labels and arrows.

figures.alt: Original five-panel comparison of generation trajectories, ending with Straight Variational Flow Matching.
figures.reason: This theory-led paper has no separate architecture or teaser. Its main Figure 1 is the method’s canonical trajectory visualization, illustrating straight generation paths rather than a metric or unrelated result plot. Complete figure and all five subfigure labels extracted from PDF page 5.

figures.alt: Original HIERAMP method figure showing a scale-restricted training mask and coarse-to-fine semantic amplification.
figures.reason: Official arXiv method overview, downloaded byte-for-byte. Its two colored panels show the attention-mask and amplification mechanisms clearly.

figures.alt: Original CAD-VAE data-flow diagram separating target, sensitive, shared, and irrelevant latent factors.
figures.reason: The original central method diagram directly shows encoder, four latent codes, prediction heads, and shared target-sensitive information. Downloaded byte-for-byte; transparent background should be displayed on white. Also verified against PDF page 3.

figures.alt: Original conditional-dependent-coupling diagram showing data-distribution learning and transition across two conceptual panels.
figures.reason: The paper’s main conceptual method figure combines distributions, conditional trajectories, and image examples. The complete two-panel figure was extracted from PDF page 6, rather than selecting a metric chart.

figures.alt: Original method comparison showing Drift Flow Matching between multi-step Flow Matching and a one-step Drift Model.
figures.reason: Official conceptual overview links the proposed method to its two limiting cases, with original distributions, arrows, equations, and labels. Downloaded byte-for-byte; full tall figure preserved.

figures.alt: fMRI-LM framework: fMRI-text descriptor construction, text-aligned tokenizer training, LLM fine-tuning and downstream instruction tuning.
figures.reason: The complete original training overview covers the paper's three stages and multimodal components; it is more representative than its performance radar plot.

figures.alt: MoRE-Brain framework with fMRI mixture-of-experts encoder, CLIP alignment, time and space routers, and brain-guided diffusion image generation.
figures.reason: The original overview combines a visual example and the full fMRI-to-image architecture, including the paper's distinctive expert routing.

figures.alt: SpaMEM benchmark overview showing synchronized scene changes and three levels of perception and spatio-temporal memory evaluation.
figures.reason: The original benchmark overview includes actual rendered scene examples, spawn/place/remove transitions, and the three evaluation levels; it communicates the contribution without relying on a results plot.

figures.alt: ICPT teaser comparing single-concept and multi-concept personalization with multi-image in-context prompt tuning.
figures.reason: The original teaser uses visual personalization examples and recognizable prompt/token structure to explain the contribution; its identity and caption match the ICPT paper.

figures.alt: Silent-LVR teaser comparing normal, random and removed latent visual tokens, with evidence that attention-based training improves visual reasoning.
figures.reason: The original teaser combines a clear token-level conceptual illustration with the paper's motivating evidence; it is the same teaser named in the official repository README.

figures.alt: M²IV teaser contrasting token-heavy multimodal in-context demonstrations with learned vectors injected into a frozen vision-language model.
figures.reason: The original teaser directly contrasts vanilla multimodal ICL and the proposed representation-engineering approach using a visual question-answering example, without substituting a newly drawn diagram.

figures.alt: ComfySearch method overview showing query-workflow data construction, validated workflow edits, uncertainty-triggered branching, and policy optimization.
figures.reason: Original high-resolution paper method figure. The complete data-construction and learning panels, trajectories, validation legend, and arrows are retained.

figures.alt: D-HSM converts video history into structured hub-and-spoke memory, then retrieves relevant evidence and recent frames for a frozen VLM.
figures.reason: Official project method image, independently matched to paper Figure 2. The video-frame examples and both memory/retrieval panels remain complete and sharp.

figures.alt: Sparse-Reslim routes weather tokens through dense early, sparse middle, and dense late stages, with deterministic ViT and generative EDM variants.
figures.reason: Original paper overview with intact three-stage routing, token legend, and deterministic/generative subpanels; large labels and weather maps provide a clear publication thumbnail.

figures.alt: UtoMe combines weather-state saliency and observation uncertainty to preserve anchors and merge redundant tokens, with three uncertainty-availability variants.
figures.reason: Official project supplies a higher-resolution copy of paper Figure 1, visually matched against arXiv main.png. Full weather maps, token-merging schematic, forecaster, and three variants are preserved.

figures.alt: Sensitivity-LoRA uses Hessian-based global and local weight sensitivity to allocate ranks to trainable low-rank matrices around frozen pretrained weights.
figures.reason: Original published ACL paper Figure 1 on PDF page 2. High-resolution rendering retains all method panels, matrices, formulas, rank-allocation details, and arrows without redrawing.
